title: Transforming Low-Grade Heat into Sustainable Cooling and Heating with Multicomponent Adsorbents
summary: Rapid growth in fossil-fuel consumption has amplified the severity of global climate issues, making the deployment of renewable energy solutions increasingly imperative. Among candidate approaches, adsorption-based technologies are attractive; however, the limited adsorption capacity and kinetic performance of traditional adsorbents constrain composite-cycle efficiency and hinder large-scale implementation. In this work, we develop and evaluate a new class of composite adsorbents prepared by impregnating metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with hygroscopic chloride salt solutions (LiCl, CaCl2, and MgCl2). Owing to their enhanced sorption characteristics, the resulting materials support an integrated adsorption cycle in which one device can simultaneously realize refrigeration, space heating, seawater desalination, and power generation. Under standard operating conditions, experiments demonstrate that MOF–vermiculite composites deliver a cooling coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.71, a heating COP (COPh) of 1.30, a specific power-generation output of 27.2 kJ/kg, and a desalination yield of 0.71 g/g. Collectively, these metrics outperform the majority of previously published results, indicating that composite adsorbents can substantially improve the efficiency and practicality of renewable energy conversion systems.

screen.tldr: MOF-based composite adsorbents with hygroscopic salts improve adsorption cooling, heating, desalination, and power-generation performance in an integrated renewable-energy device.

AI.method: The authors prepared composite adsorbents by impregnating metal-organic frameworks with hygroscopic salt solutions, specifically LiCl, CaCl2, and MgCl2, and evaluated their performance in an integrated adsorption cycle. title: All‐Inorganic Halide Perovskites/Wide‐Bandgap Semiconductors Heterojunctions for Self‐Powered Ultraviolet Photodetectors
summary: All‐inorganic halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for high‐performance UV photodetectors due to their unique optoelectronic properties. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the recent progress in all‐inorganic halide perovskites and their heterojunctions with wide‐bandgap semiconductors, with a particular focus on Type‐II heterojunction engineering. We first introduce the common wide‐bandgap semiconductors used in perovskite devices, including GaN, ZnO, TiO 2 , SnO 2 , Ga 2 O 3 , MoO x, and NiO. We then discuss the progress of Pb‐based and lead‐free halide perovskites in optoelectronic devices and their fabrication, performance, stability, and applications in heterojunction self‐powered UV photodetectors. The Type‐II heterojunction is highlighted as a key strategy to enhance charge separation and transfer, thereby improving device performance. Finally, we summarize the current achievements and challenges and provide an outlook for future research directions. This review aims to provide valuable insights for researchers working on the development of high‐performance UV photodetectors based on all‐inorganic halide perovskite/semiconductor heterojunctions.

screen.tldr: Review of all-inorganic halide perovskite/wide-bandgap semiconductor heterojunctions for self-powered UV photodetectors, emphasizing Type-II charge-separation engineering.

AI.tldr: This review summarizes progress in all-inorganic halide perovskite-based UV photodetectors, emphasizing Type-II heterojunctions with wide-bandgap semiconductors to improve charge separation, self-powered operation, and device performance.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by the need for high-performance UV photodetectors and the strong optoelectronic potential of all-inorganic halide perovskites, especially when integrated with wide-bandgap semiconductors to address efficiency and stability challenges.
AI.method: The paper is a literature review that surveys Pb-based and lead-free all-inorganic halide perovskites, common wide-bandgap partners such as GaN, ZnO, TiO2, SnO2, Ga2O3, MoOx, and NiO, and recent advances in heterojunction device fabrication, performance, and stability, with a focus on Type-II band alignment engineering.
AI.result: The review identifies Type-II heterojunction design as an effective strategy for enhancing carrier separation and transfer, which improves UV photodetector performance, particularly in self-powered configurations. AI.conclusion: All-inorganic halide perovskite/semiconductor heterojunctions are a promising platform for next-generation UV photodetectors. Future progress will likely depend on better heterojunction engineering, improved stability, and continued development of lead-free alternatives.

title: Optoelectronic, Solar Cell and Multiferroic Analysis of the Ruddlesden-Popper Perovskite MnCaTa 2 O 7 : A First Principles Study
summary: Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite MnCaTa 2 O 7 with space group P2 1nm is investigated through density functional theory. This compound has distorted structure due to tilting and rotation of different oxygen octahedrons. The calculated structural properties are found consistent with experiments. The magnetic phase optimizations and magnetic susceptibility reveal the G-type antiferromagnetic nature of the compound. The electronic properties show that this material is semiconductor with band gap 2.15 eV and the semiconducting nature is also confirmed through electrical conductivity estimation. Optical properties show that this material exists in the visible range of electromagnetic spectrum and could be used in optoelectronics and photodetectors. Using Cu/Spiro-MeOTAD/MnCaTa 2 O 7 /WS 2 /FTO as a solar cell device with Spiro-MeOTAD is HTL, MnCaTa 2 O 7 is an absorbing layer, WS 2 is ETL and FTO is the front contact, gives a solar cell properties which are useful for photovoltaic applications with corresponding values of Jsc, Voc, fill factor and power convergence efficiency are 13.60 mA/cm 2 , 1.44 V, 85.30 % and 16.71 % respectively. The Berry phase polarization for MnCaTa2O7 is 5.49 μC/cm 2 suggests that this compound could be used in electronic and spintronic devices.

screen.tldr: First-principles study of a Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite’s electronic, optical, magnetic, and photovoltaic properties, with device-level solar-cell estimates.

AI.method: First-principles density functional theory calculations were used to optimize the crystal and magnetic structure, compute magnetic susceptibility, electronic band structure, conductivity, optical response, and Berry phase polarization. A solar-cell device model was also simulated using MnCaTa2O7 as the absorber layer.
AI.result: The compound was found to have a distorted perovskite structure consistent with experiment, G-type antiferromagnetic ordering, semiconducting behavior with a 2.15 eV band gap, and optical activity in the visible range. The proposed solar-cell configuration yielded Jsc = 13.60 mA/cm2, Voc = 1.44 V, fill factor = 85.30%, and power conversion efficiency = 16.71%. The Berry phase polarization was 5.49 μC/cm2.
AI.conclusion: MnCaTa2O7 appears to be a promising multifunctional material for optoelectronic, photovoltaic, and spintronic device applications due to its stable distorted structure, antiferromagnetism, semiconducting nature, visible-light response, and nonzero polarization.
